newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurd chief says he could turn to Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd chief says he could turn to Baghdad.

text.p: Kurdish warlord Massoud Barzani on Thursday threatened to ask the Iraqi government for help in his feud with a rival militia.
"If the Kurdish people are under hard pressure of the PUK," we will ask for help from Iraq," Barzani told a news conference at his residence near the northern town of Salahuddin.
Barzani's rivals, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), have closed in this week on the city of Arbil, which Barzani's men captured with the backing of Iraqi tanks and troops in late August.
Iraqi intervention then in its northern Kurdish region prompted the United States to launch missiles at military targets in southern Iraq in reprisal.
Barzani repeated accusations that neighbouring Iran had supplied his rival group with munitions and around 13,000 men in a week-old offensive against him. Tehran denies the charges.
"If Iran has the right to support the PUK, why shouldn't we have the right to demand support from Iraq," he said.
There has been no sign of Iranian or Iraqi military presence on both sides of the Kurdish groups' lines in sporadic fighting this week.
Barzani said he was not willing to hold direct talks with PUK leader Jalal Talabani, despite U.S. mediation attempts.
Officials from the two Kurdish warring parties were to meet senior U.S. diplomat Robert Pelletreau in Washington later on Thursday.
Pelletreau will also set off soon to meet separately with Barzani and Talabani, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Wednesday.
He said Washington wanted to "convince them that it is in their immediate interest to move towards a ceasefire and not to allow Iran or Iraq the opportunity to inflame the situation further."
A U.S.-led allied air force set up to shield the Kurds from Baghdad did not try to prevent President Saddam Hussein's forces entering Arbil. It has played no part in the Kurdish conflict.

"Our core, fundamental assessment is that neither of them can win militarily on the battlefield, but we believe that by stopping the fighting and agreeing at least to work together... they can restore stability to northern Iraq and hopefully keep Iran and Iraq out," Burns said.
The PUK said in a statement that elite Iraqi government troops were moving north from Baghdad to attack its positions and urged the United States and other nations to intervene.
"We call upon the world, especially the United States, to prevent another onslaught by Saddam's forces against the people of Iraqi Kurdistan," said the statement, received in Paris.
It could not be independently confirmed.

Talabani has said he will not try to recapture Arbil, citing the presence of Iraqi armour there. But the PUK has taken two roads towards the city and some 6,000 Talabani fighters have gathered for a push near a third highway.
Senior PUK official Kosrat Rassoul said he and other leaders would meet later in the day to discuss whether to assault KDP positions around the city.
"The politburo is meeting this evening to make a decision on the attack," he told Reuters in the town of Koy Sanjak.
